second_order: playing along with a leaked reremaster prank
theme_note: The codes hold together as participants disclose, time-check, explain, imagine the cost of, and rename one fake combined release; what varies is whether they challenge the timing or extend the joke.

second_order: making fake game news for April Fools
theme_note: These codes share the practice of using anniversary dates, datamines, releases and trailers as fake news, then believing, extending, criticizing or tiring of the prank; the announced object and reactions vary.

second_order: turning the sub into Final Fantasy for April Fools
theme_note: These codes hold together as members notice, explain, praise, inhabit and point outward from the subreddit-wide Final Fantasy presentation; what varies is confusion, play-along posting, moderator rationale and attention to details.

second_order: calling for a Keyblade to represent Kingdom Hearts
theme_note: These codes share the first direct canvas practice: asking for a Keyblade representation and explaining the paint-able canvas and five-minute pixel rule; the difference is between recruitment and basic orientation.

second_order: trying and restarting a Sora sprite
theme_note: These codes enact one Sora attempt by announcing coordinates, making a coordinate-and-palette sheet, and diagnosing lack of coordination when the space fills; the practice varies from planning to abandonment.

second_order: checking whether canvas work is really shared
theme_note: These codes hold together as a maker tries to protect a drawing and another participant checks the shared record, finding it appeared only locally; the difference is claim versus correction.

second_order: getting room from neighbours for a Kingdom Key
theme_note: These codes combine reported permission from r/thebluecorner with a rapid recruitment call before a named rival swarms the area; permission and urgency vary within the same attempt.

second_order: showing a Keyblade at its coordinates
theme_note: This single-code theme keeps the distinct practice of pointing the room to a Keyblade already visible at 82, 232.

second_order: showing and losing small canvas contributions
theme_note: These codes share the practice of displaying small personal contributions, teasing or locating them, then reporting their overwriting and mourning the loss; what varies is critique, promised repair, and replacement talk.

second_order: building and keeping a Keyblade alive
theme_note: These codes hold together as participants ask for help, choose a surrounding color, urge effort, resist erasure, and report loss during one nearly finished Keyblade build; construction, visibility and defence vary.

second_order: asking permission and keeping off neighbours pixels
theme_note: These codes enact agreements and territorial rules across the Buffalo Bills, Blue Corner and Green Lattice encounters: invoking a deal, asking what to do at a collision, requesting a move, warning of removal, and requiring permission; the neighbour and consequence vary.

second_order: shrinking and relocating until a design fits
theme_note: These codes hold together as participants gauge interest, shrink designs, leave contested or chaotic sites, seek small openings and keep the plan simple; the candidate image and destination vary.

second_order: claiming a small Keyblade as ours
theme_note: This single-code theme preserves the distinct completion practice: announcing that the small inconspicuous Keyblade was finished and belonged to the group.

second_order: moving the larger Keyblade project to Discord
theme_note: This single-code theme captures inviting helpers into a larger follow-on whose discussion occurred on Discord, distinct from fitting the small design on-canvas.

second_order: directing helpers to the live Keyblade
theme_note: These codes share the practice of volunteering, redirecting people to the active coordinates, joining there, and negotiating an alternative image while keeping work together; what varies is offer, redirection and uptake.

second_order: linking the work to placekeyblades factions
theme_note: These two codes connect the local project to two days of similar factional work and point members toward r/placekeyblades; recollection and redirection vary.

second_order: starting inside the Linux penguin
theme_note: This single-code theme retains a distinct, thin canvas attempt whose deleted body leaves only the starting location in the surviving title.

second_order: having AutoModerator remove an r/place attempt
theme_note: This single-code theme keeps the community-operated rule response to a canvas attempt missing the required title tag.

second_order: adding K H, a border and a heart
theme_note: These codes share the practice of extending the completed compact Keyblade with K H, choosing border and logo colors, proposing a heart, and limiting it to avoid Megaman’s flame; the added element and constraint vary.

second_order: patching and maintaining completed pieces
theme_note: These codes hold together as participants patch an attacked heart, finish a shift, stop expanding, and repair tiles after completion; what varies is the threatened element and the maintenance rhythm.

second_order: keeping track of both Kingdom Hearts pieces
theme_note: These codes point builders from one completed work to the other and remind them to manage both, preserving the distinct practice of maintaining two simultaneous pieces.

second_order: arguing for peace instead of stomping over others
theme_note: These codes hold together as a Darkness takeover proposal is redirected, criticized as harm, reframed around collaborative expression, answered with calls for peace, and turned back toward helping the Keyblade; positions vary from proposed alliance to explicit refusal.

second_order: protecting the full-sized Keyblade to the end
theme_note: These codes hold together as participants announce the full-sized Keyblade complete, warn of a white-blob threat, thank defenders, record improvement, and mark the final position set in stone; what varies is threat, encouragement, progress and closure.

second_order: celebrating and crediting two surviving pieces
theme_note: These codes hold together as participants call for last defence, thank Reddit and Discord, claim building and maintenance through the finish, assess success, credit a neighbour’s script, answer that credit, praise the large Keyblade and sign off; what varies is contribution, evaluation and thanks.

second_order: extending and arguing over the Xion April Fools joke
theme_note: These codes hold together as participants source, perform, explain, rewrite, criticize and calendar-reason through one Xion-is-forgotten April Fools comic; what varies is playful extension, confusion, requested repair and rejection as stale karma bait.
